comparator_concept: Interactional grounding: participants try to reach the grounding criterion, mutual belief that they have understood well enough for current purposes; contributions have presentation and acceptance phases
evidence_read: Clark and Brennan PDF p. 2 and closing paragraph PDF p. 12; Clark and Schaefer abstract; Bansal et al. abstract; Clark 1996 and Brennan and Hulteen metadata only
apparent_relation_for_8: Apparent equivalence with symbol grounding (CM02) is a homonym; possible analogy with the project's situated understanding (CM04)
question_for_8: Is the project's 'adequate interpretation for appropriate action' a grounding criterion in Clark's sense, and can a one-way alert ever reach mutual belief?

comparator_concept: Symbol grounding: how symbols in a formal system get intrinsic meaning rather than meaning 'parasitic on the meanings in our heads'; reviews and objections to proposed solutions
evidence_read: Harnad abstract (arXiv record); Taddeo and Floridi and Müller metadata only
apparent_relation_for_8: Different problem from CM01 under the same word; possible tension with Brier's claim that machines lack first-person interpretation (Brier side unread here)
question_for_8: Does the project need any position on whether the machine itself interprets, or only on the listener's interpretation?

comparator_concept: Three senses: cybernetic feedback as control; conversational feedback as evidence of understanding (acknowledgement, repair); closed-loop interaction in sonification
evidence_read: Traum PDF pp. 2-4; Hermann abstract PDF p. 1 (hierarchy of closed-loop interactions); Clark and Schaefer and Schegloff et al. abstracts; Wiener and Brennan and Hulteen metadata only
apparent_relation_for_8: Analogous rather than equivalent: control loops need no shared understanding; conversational feedback does
question_for_8: Which sense does 'acknowledgement' in glossary G13 use, and does Traum's point that a contribution's state cannot be read on-line (PDF p. 3) constrain the state model in #12?

comparator_concept: Peirce's immediate, dynamic and final interpretants (explicit content apart from context; actual effect produced; the interpretation inquiry would settle on); Clark's purpose-relative criterion; modes of listening; depiction
evidence_read: Atkin paragraphs 49-56 (section 4.2); Clark and Brennan PDF p. 2; Clark and Fischer abstract; Tuuri and Eerola and Gaver metadata only
apparent_relation_for_8: Partial analogy only: the final interpretant is a norm at the end of inquiry, Clark's criterion is relative to current purposes, and K06 counts interpretive effort; none is an equivalent of another
question_for_8: Which, if any, of these supplies a usable success criterion for RQ3 and RQ6, and what does each leave out?

comparator_concept: Operational closure of autopoietic and social systems; observing systems; whether social systems are autopoietic; definitional boundary of sonification; event-alarm-action triangulation in alarm design
evidence_read: Mingers abstract; Hermann definition conditions C1-C3 PDF p. 2; Sanz-Segura et al. PDF p. 14 (onion model, alarm triangulation); others metadata only
apparent_relation_for_8: Probably incompatible senses: a self-producing system's closure versus an engineered signal chain's scope; flagged so that #8 does not equate them
question_for_8: Where does the project draw the boundary of 'the communication' (device, alarm system, care team, listener), and does Brier's use of closure add anything that the engineering boundary lacks?

comparator_concept: Auditory icons (everyday-sound resemblance) and earcons (abstract learned structure); sonification definition that covers both; deliberately unnatural or affordance-aligned robot voices; contrary evidence favouring human-like voices
evidence_read: Hermann PDF p. 2 (earcons and auditory icons fall under the definition); Kühne et al. PDF p. 1; Moore abstract; Becker et al. and Romeo et al. abstracts; others metadata only or unavailable
apparent_relation_for_8: Tension, not equivalence: the project's preference for non-human machine sound meets reports that human-like voices are liked more and can raise compliance or behavioural trust
question_for_8: Is the preference a design hypothesis to test (#13/#14) rather than a premise, and do the contrary studies enter Track E through #6?

comparator_concept: Interpretant as translation or development of the sign; determination that is not causal; divisions immediate/dynamic/final and emotional/energetic/logical, whose relation is contested
evidence_read: Atkin paragraphs 9-11 (section 1.3) and 63-67 (section 4.3, including the EP2:409 quotation that every interpretant includes feeling); Short and Parmentier metadata only
apparent_relation_for_8: Hypothesis only: if every interpretant includes feeling (EP2:409 as quoted by Atkin), 'listener affect' is not optional under a Peircean reading; this says nothing about Brier's own position, which is unread here
question_for_8: Does the project's separation of attributed machine emotion from listener affect (G23) survive a Peircean reading, and how does Brier use the emotional interpretant (#7)?

comparator_concept: Selective information of a channel; book version with Weaver's essay; 'difference that makes a difference'; semantic information as meaningful data; semantic information as information causally necessary for a system's self-maintenance
evidence_read: Kolchinsky and Wolpert abstract PDF p. 1; others metadata only
apparent_relation_for_8: Possible incompatibility: Kolchinsky and Wolpert define meaning for a system without an interpreter's interpretant; Brier treats information as an aspect of semiosis (#7 to verify)
question_for_8: Can the project use a formal semantic-information measure without contradicting its Peircean premises, or are the two accounts answering different questions?

comparator_concept: Perceived urgency as a function of acoustic parameters; psychophysical scaling of urgency; event criticality mapped to informing, warning, alarming and urging sounds and to required response times
evidence_read: Edworthy et al. and Hellier et al. abstracts; Sanz-Segura et al. PDF pp. 13-14; Edworthy and Hellier 2006 metadata only
apparent_relation_for_8: Close analogue: Sanz-Segura et al. chain criticality, alarm informativeness and compliance with response-time bands, which overlaps the project's designed, perceived and time-to-action urgency (N04, N06)
question_for_8: What does the project add beyond this framework and the urgency-mapping tradition, and is that addition testable?

comparator_concept: Uncanny valley; social responses to computers; anthropomorphism as attribution; robots as depictions of social agents; surveys and ethics reviews of agent voice
evidence_read: Kühne et al. PDF p. 1 (higher human-likeness rated less eerie, contrary to an uncanny-valley expectation); Clark and Fischer, Seaborn et al., Ferrario et al. and Mildner et al. abstracts; others metadata only
apparent_relation_for_8: Apparent equivalence to flag: 'human-likeness' bundles voice naturalness, attributed agency and the depicted character; Clark and Fischer's depiction account is a third option between 'human' and 'machine'
question_for_8: Should RQ5 separate the voice's naturalness from the agent the listener takes to be speaking?

comparator_concept: Reviewability of a medium (speech fades quickly, recorded messages remain); repair organisation; contribution state; alarm silencing and recovery in practice
evidence_read: Clark and Brennan PDF p. 8 (printed p. 141, constraint 7) and PDF p. 9 (constraints by medium); Traum PDF pp. 2-3; Sanz-Segura et al. PDF p. 11 (interview quotations on silencing after recovery); Schegloff et al. abstract
apparent_relation_for_8: Different senses under one word: message persistence in a medium versus the persistence of a monitored state; no inspected comparator models state lifecycle as a dimension
question_for_8: Is G13 a contribution, or does it re-describe acknowledgement and repair under another name?

comparator_concept: Interface as a one-shot message from designer to user (metacommunication); communicability evaluation; an earlier semiotics of interaction
evidence_read: Valente et al. abstract (R002); all others metadata only
apparent_relation_for_8: Possible equivalence to test: the project's machine-to-listener message may be a special case of semiotic engineering's metacommunication (N09)
question_for_8: What, if anything, does a cybersemiotic account add to communicability evaluation for sound?
